doctor.title: Checkup
doctor.sub: How ergo is doing on this computer: ergo itself and each plugin, checked one by one
doctor.intro: The regular checkup only looks at this machine: no network calls, no model calls, no settings changed. It may connect to the ports of local services ergo uses.

doctor.fact.node: Running Node {running}; the pi line is {expected}
doctor.fact.components: Everything that should be installed is
doctor.fact.disk: The volume holding the data folder {path} has {free} GB free (of {total} GB)
doctor.fact.externalUnregistered: No outside access is registered in the service manager; if your phone already connects, you can ignore this
doctor.fix.ports: See who holds these ports (look the port number up in netstat -ano) and close that program; or change ports.local / ports.external in config/ergo.json to two free ports and restart ergo. If another copy of ergo holds it, stop that one in the service manager first
doctor.fix.node: Ergo and pi follow pi's tested Node line (22 for now). Use the Node that ships with ergo (or install Node 22) and start ergo again
doctor.fix.pi: pi is ergo's agent core; without it ergo can't chat. Run npm ci in ergo's repository folder to install the dependencies, then restart ergo
doctor.fix.piInstalled: pi is ergo's agent core; without it ergo can't chat. The program files are incomplete and this kind of install has no npm in its program folder, so reinstall: run ergo uninstall --keep-data (your data stays), then run the install command again and ergo comes back up by itself. If you installed with Scoop or winget, uninstall and reinstall with them
doctor.fix.piNpm: pi is ergo's agent core; without it ergo can't chat. The program files are incomplete: run npm i -g ergo-ai@latest to reinstall, then restart ergo
doctor.fix.supervisor: Without the service manager nobody watches ergo (it won't come back after a crash). Run ergo start to bring it up again; if that fails, read the service manager log (%LOCALAPPDATA%\ergo\supervisor\logs\manager.log)
doctor.fix.model: Put a model key in Settings · Models (or on the second screen of the setup wizard) — DeepSeek by default, or switch to a custom OpenAI-compatible provider first; you can also drop the key into the secrets folder of the data directory and restart ergo
doctor.fix.components: Install the missing ones in Settings · Components ("Install the default components" is the quickest way). Until then the features they enable are greyed out
doctor.fix.disk: Free at least 1 GB on the volume that holds the data folder (and on the one holding the service manager's data and logs, if that's a different volume): clear old backups, download caches, logs, or move the data folder to a bigger disk
doctor.fix.external: If your phone can't connect yet: to use ergo on mobile data too, set up one of the three ways in the setup wizard's outside-access screen (Tailscale is the easiest), then pair the phone once and this check clears; if you only use it at home you can ignore this check
doctor.fix.retry: This check didn't run this time: press "Run again". If it keeps failing, look in the service manager logs (%LOCALAPPDATA%\ergo\supervisor\logs) for what ergo reported
doctor.fact.externalRejected: {base}. {count} entries can't be used by a phone: {entries}
doctor.fix.externalRejected: An entry that goes to the local port must be moved to the external port: the local port trusts requests from this computer automatically, so it must never be reachable from outside. In the service manager, change that entry's exposure.localPort or the port after the tunnel's -R. Replace non-https entries with https. Only then can a phone use the entry, and it will show up in the pairing code
doctor.summary.unknown_one: {count} more couldn't be checked this time
doctor.summary.unknown_other: {count} more couldn't be checked this time
doctor.action.compactStarted: Compaction started. Run the checkup again once it finishes
doctor.deep.title: Deep checkup
doctor.deep.hint: Sends one very short request to test the model (costs less than a cent), goes online, and takes a little while. It only runs when you tap it; the regular checkup skips these.
doctor.deep.cooldown: Just tested; you can test again in {seconds} s
doctor.deep.tooSoon: Just tested; try again in {seconds} s

doctor.check.database.title: Database integrity
doctor.check.sourceProbe.title: Live check: {name}
doctor.modelProbe.ok: {model} replied: first token in {first} s, done in {total} s
doctor.modelProbe.slow: {model} replied, but slowly: first token in {first} s, done in {total} s
doctor.modelProbe.noKey: No model key yet, so nothing was sent
doctor.modelProbe.timeout: {model} didn't finish replying within {seconds} s; the request was aborted
doctor.modelProbe.why.key: the key is wrong (the provider rejected it)
doctor.modelProbe.why.balance: out of credit (balance or quota used up)
doctor.fix.modelProbeSlow: The provider may be busy: test again in a while; if it stays this slow, switch models in Settings · Models
doctor.fix.modelProbe.timeout: The provider may be very busy or slow: test again in a while; if it keeps happening, switch models in Settings · Models
doctor.fix.modelProbe.key: Check the key in Settings · Models and enter it again; also check with the provider whether the key was disabled
doctor.fix.modelProbe.balance: Top up or check your quota with the provider; if you need it now, switch models in Settings · Models
doctor.fix.modelProbe.rate: Test again in a while; if you keep getting rate-limited, switch models in Settings · Models or raise your limit with the provider
doctor.fix.modelProbe.busy: The provider is busy: test again in a while, or switch models in Settings · Models
doctor.fix.modelProbe.network: Check that this computer is online and whether it needs a proxy; for a custom provider, check the endpoint in Settings · Models
doctor.fix.modelProbe.other: Tap Test in Settings · Models to see the full reason and fix that, or switch models
doctor.database.ok: ergo.db is intact ({size}, checked in {seconds} s)
doctor.fix.database: Don't delete or move the data folder yet: make a backup in Settings · Backup first, then follow "How to restore" on that page to restore the latest good snapshot
doctor.sourceProbe.unconfigured: Not set up yet, so not tested: {reason}
doctor.fix.sourceProbe.auth: Open it in Settings · Data sources, enter the key again and test the connection
doctor.fix.sourceProbe.rateLimit: Test again in a minute; syncs wait on their own
doctor.fix.sourceProbe.network: Check that this computer is online and whether it needs a proxy, then test again in a while
doctor.fix.sourceProbe.timeout: Their side may be slow: test again in a while
doctor.fix.sourceProbe.server: Most likely a temporary problem on their side: test again in a while; if it persists, wait for them to fix it
doctor.fix.sourceProbe.response: Test again in a while; if it persists, they may have changed their API—wait for an ergo update
doctor.unknown.timeout: Couldn't check this time: not done within {seconds} seconds
doctor.unknown.failed: Couldn't check this time: the check failed ({message})
doctor.unknown.bad: Couldn't check this time: the result didn't make sense
doctor.plugin.title: The plugin itself
doctor.plugin.missing: An external component it needs isn't installed: {reason}
doctor.fix.pluginSkipped: Check the reason in Settings · Plugins, fix it, then enable the plugin there (or restart ergo)
doctor.source.title: Data source: {name}
doctor.pluginOff: The plugin isn't loaded, so this wasn't checked
doctor.source.manual: Imported through the import folder, last on {time}
doctor.source.manualNever: Imported through the import folder, nothing imported yet
doctor.source.stale: No successful sync for {hours} hours (scheduled import: {schedule})
doctor.fix.sourceAuth: Open it in Settings · Data sources and authorize again, or enter the key again
doctor.fix.sourceError: Open it in Settings · Data sources to see why it failed; ergo retries it every hour
doctor.fix.sourceSync: Open it in Settings · Data sources and press "Sync now" to see whether it still fails
doctor.runtime.title: Runtime: {name}
doctor.runtime.missing: Not installed (no task or project uses it): {reason}
doctor.runtime.missingUsed_one: Not installed, but {count} task or project uses it: {reason}
doctor.runtime.missingUsed_other: Not installed, but {count} tasks or projects use it: {reason}
doctor.fix.runtimeMissing: Install it as described above, then enable it in Settings · Plugins; until then the tasks and projects that use it are on hold
doctor.source.off: Connected, but both uses are off, so not checked
doctor.source.staleFailed: No successful sync for {hours} hours (scheduled import: {schedule}); the last attempt failed: {error}

doctor.assistant.restarting: {name} just exited and is being restarted
doctor.assistant.why.restarting: it exited unexpectedly and is waiting to be restarted
doctor.fix.assistant: Wait a moment and run the checkup again. If it stays offline, look at "Model calls lately" and "Conversation length" (an unreachable model or an overlong conversation can keep it from starting); if that doesn't help, restart ergo in the service manager (ergo start)
doctor.modelCalls.someFailed: Last 15 minutes: {failed} of {total} turn(s) failed ({gists}), under 30%
doctor.modelCalls.allFailed: The last {n} turns all failed: {gists}; the latest at {time} ({model})
doctor.modelCalls.quiet: No calls in the last 15 minutes; the previous turn was at {time}: {outcome}
doctor.modelCalls.gist.busy: the provider says it's too busy
doctor.modelCalls.gist.auth: the key is wrong or lacks permission
doctor.modelCalls.gist.overflow: the conversation outgrew the model's window
doctor.fix.modelCalls: The provider may be busy: wait a while, or switch to another model in Settings · Models
doctor.fix.modelCallsKey: Check the key in Settings · Models; if the key is right, check your balance and quota with the provider
doctor.fix.modelCallsOverflow: The conversation is too long: see "Conversation length" and press "Compact now"
doctor.context.over: {name}: the conversation is at {used} tokens, past its auto-compaction point of {at}, and hasn't been compacted (model window {window})
doctor.context.full: {name}: the conversation is at {used} tokens, {percent}% of the model's {window} window; any longer and it can't go on
doctor.context.autoFailed: {name}: the last automatic compaction ({time}) failed: {message}; now at {used} tokens
doctor.fix.context: Press "Compact now" and run the checkup again afterwards; if compaction keeps failing, look at "Model calls lately" (compacting calls the model too)
doctor.fix.contextFull: Press "Compact now"; if that doesn't bring it down, clear the current conversation from its ⚙ (old messages are kept)
doctor.services.noSnapshot: The service manager isn't answering, so its services can't be seen
doctor.services.none: Nothing in the service manager that ergo uses
doctor.services.stateWithError: {state}; last error recorded by the service manager: {error}
doctor.services.stateAutostart: {state}, though it's set to start at boot
doctor.fix.services: Start it in the service manager ("Open service manager" only works on this computer); if it won't start, read the error and logs it recorded
doctor.fix.servicesNoLink: Start it in the service manager (lsm start <service id>, or the service manager's web page); if it won't start, read the error and logs it recorded
doctor.plugins.fine: {running} plugin(s) running; every enabled plugin loaded
doctor.plugins.skipped: {names} failed to load (the reason is in its section below)
doctor.web.fine: The web page files are in place
doctor.web.missing: The web page files are missing: {path}
doctor.fix.web: Running from source: run npm run build:web in the repository root. Installed program: the files are incomplete; run ergo uninstall --keep-data (your data stays), then run the install command again
doctor.fact.supervisorLinkWaiting: {base}, but ergo's link to it is down and reconnecting
doctor.fix.supervisorLink: If the service manager just restarted, ergo reconnects by itself within seconds; run the checkup again. If it stays disconnected, restart ergo in the service manager (ergo start)
doctor.fact.diskSupervisor: {base}; the volume holding the service manager's data and logs {path} has {free} GB free (of {total} GB)
doctor.fact.externalUnreachable: {base}. {bad} of {total} entries can't be reached from outside: {entries}
doctor.fact.externalUnreachableAll: {base}. None of the entries can be reached from outside: {entries}
doctor.fact.externalLinkWaiting: {base}. Ergo's link to the service manager is down, so whether the entries work is from before it dropped
doctor.fix.externalUnreachable: The service manager can't reach this entry from outside: check under "Managed services" whether the outside tunnel and the tailnet gateway are running, and whether Tailscale is signed in on this computer; once fixed, the service manager tests it again and the phone can connect

doctor.backup.skipped_other: The last backup ({time}) succeeded, but {count} files held by other programs were left out: {files}
doctor.backup.skippedNoList_one: The last backup ({time}) succeeded, but {count} file held by another program was left out
doctor.backup.skippedNoList_other: The last backup ({time}) succeeded, but {count} files held by other programs were left out
doctor.fix.backupFailed: Open Settings · Backup to see why the last backup failed; fix it, then press "Back up now"
doctor.fix.backupStale: Press "Back up now" in Settings · Backup; if an external scheduler runs your backups, check whether that scheduled task has stopped

doctor.fix.backupVerify: Press "Check the latest snapshots" in Settings · Backup to check again; if it still fails, press "Back up now" to make a fresh one
doctor.triggers.ok: None paused automatically, no stuck runs
doctor.triggers.paused_one: "{title}" failed {count} time in a row and was paused automatically (last: {reason})
doctor.triggers.paused_other: "{title}" failed {count} times in a row and was paused automatically (last: {reason})
doctor.triggers.pausedNoReason_one: "{title}" failed {count} time in a row and was paused automatically
doctor.triggers.pausedNoReason_other: "{title}" failed {count} times in a row and was paused automatically
doctor.triggers.running: A run of "{title}" has been running since {time} ({duration})
doctor.triggers.queued: A run of "{title}" has been queued for {duration} without starting
doctor.fix.triggers: Open it on the board (or on its project page) to see what happened: for an auto-paused one, fix the cause and press "Resume"; for a stuck one, check what its owner is waiting for
doctor.internalJobs.ok_one: The last run of the {count} registered job finished
doctor.internalJobs.ok_other: The last runs of all {count} registered jobs finished
doctor.fix.internalJobs: It runs again when it's next due; if it keeps failing, send these lines and ergo's log from the service manager to the developers
doctor.stuckAgents.full: {live} agents are running at once, close to the limit of {max}
doctor.stuckAgents.fullQueued: {live} agents are running at once, close to the limit of {max}, and {queued} more are waiting
doctor.stuckAgents.fixStuck: Open its conversation to see what it's doing; if it's really stuck, press "Stop" next to the input box, then ask it to carry on
doctor.stuckAgents.fixFull: When too many agents run at once, new ones wait in line: wait a bit, or raise agents.maxLive in config/ergo.json (each agent uses memory)
doctor.fix.logSize: The service manager doesn't split logs yet: stop the service that writes this file in the service manager, delete or move the file, then start the service again (ergo-daemon.out.log is ergo's own: stop ergo before deleting it)
doctor.configFiles.ok: MCP registrations and model settings read fine, and every MCP has the credentials it needs
doctor.configFiles.mcp: The MCP registrations can't be read, so none of the registered MCPs work: {problem}
doctor.configFiles.model: The model settings file {file} can't be read, so defaults are in use: {error}
doctor.configFiles.mcpEnv: MCP "{name}" needs credentials that aren't in ergo's environment: {variables}
doctor.configFiles.fixMcp: Fix mcp.json (the .history folder next to it keeps a copy from before each change)
doctor.configFiles.fixModel: Save once in Settings · Models to overwrite it with fresh settings
doctor.configFiles.fixMcpEnv: Add these environment variables to ergo's registration (ergo-daemon) in the service manager, then restart ergo

doctor.missingSkills.collection: In the list of the "{collection}" collection but not in the library: {names}
doctor.missingSkills.list: Listed in {where} but not in the library: {names}
doctor.missingSkills.fixCollection: For a collection: import it again, or remove them from its list on the skills page
doctor.missingSkills.fixList: For a toolkit or list: remove it there, or import it into the skill library
doctor.pending.withApprovals_one: {count} item in the inbox, {approvals} of them waiting for approval
doctor.pending.withApprovals_other: {count} items in the inbox, {approvals} of them waiting for approval
doctor.appVersion.noDevices: No paired phone, so not checked
doctor.appVersion.noReports: Paired phones haven't reported an app version yet

doctor.appVersion.old_other: The app on {count} phones is older than the required {min}: {devices}
doctor.fix.appVersion: Update the app on that phone using the banner at the top of the app
doctor.fix.dbWal: ergo folds it back into the database when it restarts; if it's still this big after a restart, tell the developers
